clue.text: Robinson Crusoe found a track

parts.note: to found metal is to cast it in a mould
a track or path is a way

explanation.surface: Defoe's shipwrecked hero comes across a path on his island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found' looks like the past tense of find, but here it is the verb to found, as in a foundry, meaning to cast.
explanation.definitionFit: Crusoe is literature's best-known shipwrecked sailor marooned alone on an island.

clue.text: A Greek Island doctor's creation

parts.note: Cos (Kos) is a Greek island in the Dodecanese
MO, medical officer, is a doctor; with the possessive it gives MOS

explanation.surface: Something made by a physician on a Greek isle.
explanation.definitionFit: The ordered universe, all of creation, is the whole created world.

clue.text: Making a start -—- making the beds

indicators.note: making something out of the words a start signals rearranging them

explanation.surface: Getting going on household chores by making the beds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making the beds' looks domestic; the beds are geological layers.
explanation.definitionFit: Layers of rock deposited one above another are called beds.

clue.text: Bill repeatedly raised excellent mimosa

indicators.note: repeatedly tells us the bill abbreviation appears twice

parts.note: AC, account, is a bill

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the word for excellent is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: A1 means excellent, written here with an I for the one

explanation.surface: A man named Bill keeps growing a fine flowering shrub.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 (top-class) is written AI, so 'raised' turns it to IA.
explanation.definitionFit: Wattles and mimosas belong to the same genus of yellow-flowered trees.

clue.text: There's a total lack of choice still

definitions.text: There's a total lack of choice
definitions.meaning: every option is identical, so it makes no difference

explanation.definitionFit: Identical options give no real choice, and the phrase also means nevertheless.

clue.text: Opposing article with snappy follow-up

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
snappy, irritable and short-tempered means cross

explanation.surface: An opposing newspaper piece draws a sharp reply.
explanation.definitionFit: Something across from you is facing or opposite you, set on the other side.

clue.text: The person with a consuming interest in his own kind

definitions.text: The person with a consuming interest in his own kind

parts.words: The person with a consuming interest in his own kind
parts.note: a consuming interest sounds like obsession, but literally means eating one's own species

explanation.surface: Someone passionately interested in people like themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: A man-eater eats human flesh, devouring members of its own species.

clue.text: Actor finding love through a. "rubbish" write-up

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like O
per means through or by means of

indicators.note: write-up in a down clue means the words a rubbish are written upwards, backwards

parts.note: rubbish, nonsense, is rot

explanation.surface: A performer finds romance via a rubbish review.
explanation.walkthrough: 'write-up' looks like a review; in a down clue it reverses A ROT to TORA.
explanation.definitionFit: One who acts or works a machine, a performer of an action, is an actor in the wide sense.

clue.text: In the main this Is not mounted

definitions.text: In the main this Is not mounted

parts.words: In the main this Is not mounted
parts.note: in the main means mostly, but here it is the sea, where this creature is a steed nobody rides

explanation.surface: Generally speaking, this is not ridden.
explanation.walkthrough: The main is an old word for the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A small fish with a horselike head, living in the sea.

clue.text: Changes are silly, though, made one after another

indicators.note: the word changes tells us the letters that follow are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Silly alterations nonetheless get made in sequence.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing things serially means doing them in a series, each following the last.

clue.text: She shows endless irritation with the French

indicators.note: endless asks us to cut the final letter off the word for irritation

parts.note: irritation, being riled, is anger
la is the French feminine word for the

explanation.surface: A woman displays constant annoyance with the French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' removes the last letter of ANGER, leaving ANGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, so any woman bearing it can be referred to as she.

clue.text: Striking Conservatives as sweeping

parts.note: workers who are striking are out on strike
the political right means the conservatives

explanation.surface: Industrial action by Tory supporters is described as wide-ranging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Striking' looks like an adjective meaning impressive; it is the strike sense, OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweeping victory is a complete, total, unqualified one.

clue.text: It's fruit or a turnover for this opera-singer

parts.note: the fig is a fruit

indicators.note: a turnover flips the words or a so that they are read backwards

explanation.surface: Whether fruit or pastry is offered, it is for this singer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turnover' looks like a pastry beside 'fruit'; it reverses OR A to ARO.
explanation.definitionFit: The barber of Seville is a title role sung on stage in operas by Rossini and Mozart.

clue.text: Many a woman with over round body is very fast

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, i.e. many
Ann is a woman's name
over, as in a dispute over money, means on, concerning
a ball is a round body

explanation.surface: Many a woman with a round figure is very quick.
explanation.definitionFit: A cannon's shot travels at great speed, so a cannonball express is a high-speed one.

clue.text: On-going means of coping with ups and downs

definitions.text: On-going means of coping with ups and downs

parts.words: On-going means of coping with ups and downs
parts.note: the clue reads like advice on enduring life's vicissitudes, but literally describes moving stairs that carry you up and down as you go on them

explanation.surface: A continuing method of handling life's highs and lows.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving staircases literally carry people up and down between floors as they step on.

clue.text: A Swiss place where married people come in awfully late

indicators.note: come in tells us the married people go inside the other letters
awfully suggests the word late is rearranged

parts.note: people, as in chaps, are men

explanation.surface: Married couples arrive terribly late at a Swiss location.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' rearranges LATE to ETAL; MMEN goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A valley in the canton of Bern gives its name to the holey cheese.

clue.text: Profit from intrigue?

definitions.meaning: to intrigue is to arouse curiosity

explanation.definitionFit: Money earned on a loan is a return, and to fascinate someone is to arouse their curiosity.

clue.text: Middle-men appear nice maybe in time

indicators.note: in tells us the anagram goes inside the word for time

parts.note: a long time is ages

indicators.note: maybe suggests the word nice is rearranged

explanation.surface: Intermediaries seem pleasant, perhaps, given time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' rearranges NICE to ENCI, placed inside AGES.
explanation.definitionFit: Firms that act on behalf of others are intermediaries between client and supplier.

clue.text: Being game, ten perhaps will be in the running

parts.note: a human being is a man

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the words game and ten may be rearranged

explanation.surface: Being up for it, ten candidates may be in contention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the running' looks like contention in a race; 'the running' is the running of a business.
explanation.definitionFit: The people who run a firm, or the act of directing it, is its administration.

clue.text: Having a bawl

parts.note: sounds like having a ball, enjoying oneself, but it is a weeping fit

explanation.definitionFit: To bawl is to weep loudly, shedding tears noisily.

clue.text: Some like to paint, entirely absorbed

indicators.note: some tells us only part of the words paint, entirely is taken

explanation.surface: Some people love painting and become wholly engrossed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone intent on a task is engrossed and concentrating hard.

clue.text: A tree's In need of shaping, and that can be problem

indicators.note: a tree needing shaping, like pruning, signals rearranging the letters

explanation.surface: A tree that needs pruning can be a headache.
explanation.definitionFit: A brain-teaser is a puzzle or tricky question.

clue.text: Players ordered off

parts.note: the clue suggests sportsmen sent off by a referee, but describes a stage direction telling actors to leave

explanation.surface: Sportsmen are sent off the field.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the Latin stage direction for actors to depart, literally 'they go out'.

clue.text: Send for a drive?

definitions.meaning: to send someone is to delight or enrapture them, putting them in a trance
the gateway or way in to a driveway

explanation.definitionFit: To enrapture is to captivate a listener, and a gateway is the way into a driveway.

clue.text: The point is there's a proposition to be maintained

parts.note: S, south, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: The key thing is an argument needing to be upheld.
explanation.definitionFit: A dissertation's central argument is a claim the writer defends.

clue.text: Measuring instruments for the production of replicas

indicators.note: the production of something new out of the word replicas signals rearranging its letters

explanation.surface: Gauges used to make copies.
explanation.definitionFit: Hinged gauges with two legs measure the thickness or diameter of objects.

clue.text: Somewhat overdue note about back-rest

indicators.note: about tells us the note wraps around the other piece

parts.note: lah is the sixth note in tonic sol-fa

indicators.note: back tells us the word for rest is read backwards

parts.note: to rest is to sit

explanation.surface: Something a bit late concerns the back support of a chair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back-rest' looks like part of a chair; 'back' reverses SIT to TIS, which goes inside LAH.
explanation.definitionFit: The suffix -ish means rather, so it is rather late, a little behind time.

clue.text: The fellow's second-rate of less consequence

definitions.meaning: a person who slights others, treating them as second-rate
comparative of slight, meaning less important

explanation.walkthrough: Read 'second-rate' as a verb: the fellow who rates others second, i.e. snubs them, is one who slights.
explanation.definitionFit: One who snubs disparages people, and a more trivial matter is less weighty.
